title: Data
status: draft: written 18 Nov 2026 offline for Grade 4; not yet checked by a Kenyan maths teacher; not loaded by the live tutor
notes: Outcomes a to e are KICD's words (verified); f attitudinal. Data are collected at school, at most 10 items, and recorded in a table; no graphs are asked in Grade 4. Collecting data (b) is hands-on and stays with the teacher; the skills here read and use a table. HOREB's earlier skill title said 'Bar Graphs & Tables'; graphs are not in the design for this grade.

skills.key_step: The child chooses tally marks, counters and a table to collect and record data, drawing tallies in gates of five with the fifth stroke across.

floor.question: Count the learners in your row.

representations: tally marks in gates of five
steps: Make a tally mark for each one.
Cross every fifth mark over the four before it.
Write the totals in a table.
contexts: counting cars at the school gate
birds seen in the school garden

board.do: Count them with the child: one, two, three, four.
Ask: where does the fifth stroke go?
Draw the fifth stroke across the four: one gate is 5.

misconceptions.repair: Make a gate: four and one across.

misconceptions.ask: What do we use to record counts?
How many strokes are in a gate?
What if you lose count at 23?
Is each fruit written once with its count?

checks.question: Show 8 with tally marks.
checks.answer: one gate of five and III

checks.question: What can you use to record how many learners like each fruit?

skills.key_step: The child asks or counts every member of the group once, records as they go, and keeps to at most 10 items.

floor.question: Count the chairs in a row without missing any.

steps: Choose a question with at most 10 answers.
Ask or count each member once.
Tick or tally as you go.
Check nobody was missed or counted twice.

board.do: Draw a class list with tick boxes.
The child ticks names as each one answers.

misconceptions.repair: Yes: tick names to stop that.

misconceptions.ask: How many items can our table hold?
Did everyone in the class answer?
Did you count the back rows?

checks.question: How can you make sure nobody is counted twice?
checks.answer: tick each name on the class list

checks.question: Why ask every learner, not only your friends?
checks.answer: so the data is for the whole class

skills.key_step: The child draws a table with headings, puts each item once, records tallies and writes the totals as numbers.

floor.prerequisite: Tally marks in gates of five.
floor.question: How many is one gate and II?

representations: a table with Item, Tally and Total columns
steps: Count each tally and write the total.

board.do: Draw a table: Fruit, Tally, Total.
Write mango with two gates and III.

misconceptions.ask: How many marks are in a gate?
How many kinds were in the survey?
How many marks in each gate?

checks.question: A tally shows three gates and I. What is the total?
What headings does a table of favourite fruits need?

skills.key_step: The child reads the number beside each item, compares numbers for most and least, subtracts for how many more and adds every row for a total.
steps: Find the row or rows it asks about.
Most or least: compare the numbers.
How many more: subtract; in all: add every row.
contexts: fruits sold at the school canteen

board.do: Draw a table: mangoes 8, oranges 12, bananas 5.

misconceptions.ask: Is the last row the biggest number?
Did I ask which game or how many?

checks.question: Mangoes 9, oranges 6, bananas 11. How many more bananas than oranges?
Same table: how many fruits in all?
